J.'''" '''O'Brien''' (born April 8, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Tofaş S.K.|Tofaş]] of [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State Aztecs]] and the [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah Utes]]. ==High school career== O'Brien attended the [[Alta Loma High School]] in [[Rancho Cucamonga, California]]. As a senior, he averaged 24 points, 7.4 rebounds and 2.1 steals, earning a first-team all-league selection, being nominated for the McDonald's All-American and ended as Alta Loma's all-time leading scorer with 2,200 points.{{cite news|url=http://www.utahutes.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/obrien_jj00.html|title=20 J.J. O'Brien|work=UtahUtes.com|access-date=August 29, 2015|archive-date=January 29, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160129182329/http://www.utahutes.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/obrien_jj00.html|url-status=dead}} ==College career== O'Brien began his basketball career with [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]]. In his freshman season, he played in 22 games starting 21 averaging 6.4 points, 5.5 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 27.7 minutes after missing 9 games due to a broken foot.{{cite news|url=http://www.goaztecs.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jj_obrien_796211.html|title=20 J.J. O'Brien|work=GoAztecs.com|access-date=August 29, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150922003449/http://www.goaztecs.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jj_obrien_796211.html|archive-date=September 22, 2015|url-status=dead}} The next year, O'Brien transferred to [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]] and sat out that season. On his sophomore season, he played in all 34 games, starting 33 averaging 7.2 points on 52.6 percent shooting, 4.5 rebounds and 1.5 assists. He scored in double figures in 10 of his final 16 outings, including six of his final 11 games, ending with 13 double-figures scoring. He was the Mountain West Player of the Week on January 28. As a junior, O'Brien played and started 35 of 36 games averaging a career-high 7.8 points and 4.7 rebounds also setting career highs in minutes played (27.9), free-throw percentage (.644) and three-point field-goal percentage (.278). All of this earned him an All-Mountain West Honorable Mention. As a senior with the Aztecs, O'Brien averaged 10.3 points, 5.2 rebounds and 2.4 assists.{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-free-agent-j.j.-obrien|title=Jazz Sign Free Agent J.J. O'Brien|work=NBA.com|date=August 28, 2015|access-date=August 29, 2015}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2015 NBA draft]], O'Brien joined the [[Utah Jazz]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League|Utah Summer League]], where he saw action in all three games, averaging 4.0 points and 2.3 rebounds in 13.0 minutes. He also played with Utah at the Las Vegas Summer League, owning averages of 4.6 points, 1.8 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 18.8 minutes. On August 28, 2015, he signed with the Jazz, but was later waived by the team on October 13 after appearing in one preseason game.{{cite news|title=Jazz Waive Cooley and O'Brien|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-waive-cooley-and-obrien|access-date=October 13, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2015}} On November 1, 2015, he was acquired by the [[Idaho Stampede]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Jazz.{{cite news|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5065740|title=Idaho Stampede Finalize 2015 Training Camp Roster|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 1, 2015|access-date=November 1, 2015}} On November 13, he made his professional debut in a 110–106 loss to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]], recording 12 points, three rebounds, two steals and two blocks in 42 minutes.{{cite news|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151113/IDARGV/|title=Walker Blocks Six Shots, McDaniels Scores 16 in Vipers' 110-106 Home Opener Win|work=NBA.com|date=November 13, 2015|access-date=April 4, 2016}} On January 16, 2016, O'Brien signed a 10-day contract with the Jazz.{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-jj-obrien-10-day-contract|title=Jazz Sign JJ O'Brien to 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=January 16, 2016|access-date=January 16, 2016}} Later that night, he made his NBA debut against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], recording one rebound and one steal in four minutes of action.[8] On January 26, he returned to Idaho after his contract with the Jazz expired. At the season's end, he earned NBA D-League All-Rookie Team honors.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-16-all-nba-dleague-teams-release/|title=NBA Development League Announces 2015-16 All-NBA D-League Teams|work=NBA.com|date=April 29, 2016|access-date=April 30, 2016|archive-date=September 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160904054918/http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-16-all-nba-dleague-teams-release/|url-status=dead}} In July 2016, O'Brien re-joined the [[Utah Jazz]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League|Utah Summer League]], and then played for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] at the Las Vegas Summer League. On September 8, 2016, he signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]],{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-orlando-johnson-and-jj-obrien|title=BUCKS SIGN ORLANDO JOHNSON AND J.J. O'BRIEN|work=NBA.com|date=September 8, 2016|access-date=September 8, 2016}} but was waived on October 22 after appearing in five preseason games.{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=19846|title=Bucks waive Orlando Johnson, J.J. O'Brien and Jaleel Roberts|work=InsideHoops.com|date=October 22, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161023144200/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=19846|archive-date=October 23, 2016|url-status=dead}} On October 31, he was re-acquired by the now [[Salt Lake City Stars]].{{cite web|url=http://www.slcdunk.com/2016/10/31/13478502/nba-development-league-utah-jazz-salt-lake-city-stars-jaylen-bland-carl-ona-embo-jarelle-reischel|title=Salt Lake City Stars roster and info after D-League Draft|work=SLCDunk.com|publisher=SB-Nation|date=October 31, 2016|access-date=November 5, 2016}} On August 23, 2017, O'Brien was selected by the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]] in the NBA G League expansion draft. He averaged 15.9 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game with the Clippers.{{cite web |title=JJ O'Brien signs with PBC Astana |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cups/vtb-league/284925/jj-o-brien-signs-with-pbc-astana.html |website=Sportando |access-date=August 7, 2018 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} On August 7, 2018, O'Brien signed with [[BC Astana]] in Kazakhstan. He signed with [[AS Monaco Basket|Monaco]] of the [[LNB Pro A]] in 2019. O'Brien averaged 12.5 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game, shooting 52% from the field and 74% from the foul line. He re-signed with the team on July 16, 2020.{{cite news |title=J.J. O'Brien re-signs with AS Monaco |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/j-j-obrien-re-signs-with-as-monaco/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 16, 2020 |date=July 16, 2020|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} On November 11, 2022, he signed with [[Nanterre 92]] of the [[LNB Pro A|French Pro A]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/France/news/777520/Nanterre-lands-J.J.-O'Brien|title=Nanterre lands J.J. O'Brien|last=|first=|date=November 11, 2022|website=|publisher=Eurobasket|language=En|access-date=November 11, 2022}} On July 4, 2023, he signed with [[Tofaş S.K.|Tofaş]] of [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=http://tofasspor.com/haber-2852-j_j_obrien_tofasta|title=J.
